certificationScope: non-certifying exact source-head ARM64 package and live VM smoke receipt for native media packaging and shell reliability fixes
sourceDescription: Exact source-head Linux parity follow-up containing keyboard-navigable Appearance radios, stale Computer Use authority/poll fencing, Activity snapshot retention across transient refresh failures, contained pet fallback after X11 companion errors, stale signed-update result retention, a package wrapper that forces the native GStreamer Mercury viewer feature, and a stable SmartHub bounded-output guard/test fixture. The package reused the previously verified clean daemon and CLI payloads from 2ad3b2752d; no daemon or CLI source changed in this shell wave.

limitations: The package is locally built and unsigned; it is not release provenance evidence.
The clean unlocked launch proves the exact ARM64 package renders on Ubuntu GNOME/X11, but does not certify every route, onboarding interaction, accessibility matrix, or full visual parity.
This guest does not certify WebGL2-only kernels, KDE/Wayland/wlroots, x86_64, or cross-device workflows.

The focused Linux gateway test target compiled on the guest but its executable link was blocked by the VM Swift 6.1 toolchain's missing swift::threading::fatal symbol; host execution remains blocked by the existing SQLCipher.framework rpath issue.
The strict ledger remains 0/40 product requirements and 0/7 environment receipts.
The media-enabled Tauri library gate passed 130/130 on the Ubuntu ARM64 guest; this is a focused native test/build result, not a complete cross-platform certification ledger.

This shell-only package reused the staged daemon/CLI payload from the clean 2ad3b2752d receipt; it does not replace a clean cross-layer build or signed release build. Native GStreamer linkage and plugin discovery were verified in the Ubuntu guest, but an end-to-end cross-device Mercury stream was not exercised in this bounded receipt.
